help.rules.title: Track rules
help.rules.explanation:
Every file runs the rules from the top. For each track, the first rule that fits it and keeps or drops it decides; a later rule only handles what the earlier ones left alone, and a track no rule decides is kept.

A rule fits a track when every test in its Match part is true; a test left empty is not checked.

Pausing a rule keeps it in the list but stops it from fitting anything, until it is resumed.
help.rules.example: Rule 1 drops audio named Commentary. Rule 2 keeps English audio. An English commentary track fits both, and rule 1 comes first, so it is dropped. With the two rules swapped, the same track is kept, because rule 2 now decides first. Pause rule 1 and it is kept too.
help.first_kept.title: First kept
help.first_kept.explanation:
A rule can give the default or forced flag to the first track it keeps, instead of to every track it fits. First is counted in the new file's order, so a track dragged ahead of the others takes the flag, and the other tracks of that kind lose it.

On a chip, D is the default flag and F is the forced flag; a chip or column fits one track, so First kept matters for a rule that fits several.
help.first_kept.example: A file has three English audio tracks: English 5.1, English 2.0 and English Descriptive. A rule keeps English audio and sets the default flag to First kept. D goes to English 5.1, the first one kept, and the other two have no D. If the 5.1 track is dropped, English 2.0 gets it.
help.exclude.title: Exclude
help.exclude.explanation:
Exclude leaves a show, season, episode, movie or folder out of every run until it is included again. Its files are not changed, and the exclusion is saved with the workspace.

A folder excludes everything inside it, and a place inside can be included again on its own: the nearest place decides.

It is not Remove from list, which takes a place out of the library's list altogether until its folder is added again; an excluded place stays listed, with its mark.

It is not unticking a file or a kind of change in Review, which skips it in this run only; it stays planned. It is not Discard changes either, which removes the choices made on a place and keeps it in the runs.
help.exclude.example: Exclude Show Name (2020), then include Season 2. Season 1 and its episodes stay out of every run, and Season 2 is applied as usual. Unticking Episode One in Review skips that file in this run only.
help.keep.title: Keep these files as they are
help.keep.explanation:
Keep these files as they are, in the library's right-click menu, stops what a show, a season or the Movies group sets from reaching one season, episode or movie. Its files then stay as they are, while every other place keeps the choices it receives. A choice made on the kept place itself still applies, and what only says how a change is made (custom tokens, Replace values, where originals go) still comes from above, so the place's own templates can use it.

It is a choice of that place like any other: a line under the tabs says so, the fields it cancels read Overrides the show, and Discard changes on the place takes it back, so it follows what is above again. Nothing above it changes.
help.keep.example: Show Name (2020) drops the commentary and sets a file title. Keep these files as they are on Season 2 leaves its files untouched, and Season 1 still drops the commentary. Discard changes on Season 2 makes it follow the show again.
help.queue.title: Settings kept when added
help.queue.explanation:
Add to queue plans the place at once, with each file's settings as they are at that moment, the groups and files left out of this run included, and keeps that plan. A later change in the workspace does not reach an item already queued; to queue a place with new settings, add it again: a waiting item for the same files is replaced.

When the item runs, each file is checked first. A file that changed on disk after it was queued is not written: its item says so, and adding the place again plans it from the file as it is now.

Pause lets the running step end and starts nothing more. The queue is kept when the app closes and comes back paused; Start goes on with an item that stopped part way.
help.queue.example: Season 1 is queued with the commentary dropped. Keeping the commentary afterwards changes Season 1 in the workspace, but the queued item still drops it. Add Season 1 to the queue again and the waiting item is replaced by one that keeps it.
help.replace_values.title: Replace values
help.replace_values.explanation: A token puts a value read from the file into the name, such as the name of the audio codec. A row here says: when the token reads exactly this value, write this text instead. The whole value must match, with the same letters, and a value with no row is written as it is.
help.replace_values.example: The row Dolby Digital Plus → DDP changes a file whose token reads Dolby Digital Plus to DDP in its name. A file that reads DTS is not touched.
help.discard.title: Discard changes
help.discard.explanation: Discard changes removes the choices made on this place and on the places inside it, so each follows the place above it again. Nothing is written to a file, and the places stay in the runs; Exclude is the way to leave one out. It asks first, naming what goes, and cannot be undone.
help.discard.example: Season 1 drops the commentary tracks, and one of its episodes sets its own default subtitle. Discard changes on Season 1 removes both, and every episode follows the show's choices again. The show and its other seasons keep theirs.
help.names.title: Names under a chip
help.names.explanation:
A chip groups tracks that are alike, and their names can still differ. When they do, each name is listed with the files that use it. A click on a name keeps or drops the tracks with that name and leaves the rest of the chip as it is; another click goes back, and the name follows the chip again.

Tracks without a name are listed one line per file. A click on one keeps or drops that file's track only: it is the file's own choice, which stands over what the file receives from its season or show, and Discard changes on the file removes it.

The choice is a rule in the Rules panel, placed ahead of the chip's own choice, so it decides for that name only. Discard changes removes it with the place's other choices.
help.names.example: The Dolby Digital 2.0 chip holds Commentary with the director and Commentary with the cast. Drop the chip and both go. Click Commentary with the director to keep it, and it stays while the other commentary is dropped.
help.separators.title: Separators between tokens
help.separators.explanation:
Drag a separator between two tokens, or click it to add it at the end. It goes into the template as a character, the same as typing it, and a middle click on it in the template takes it out.

Tokens and separators join themselves: the choice “Join words with” under the template puts a space, a dot, an underscore or a dash between two neighbours, so two tokens side by side read as Show Name 1x01. A dash has the join character on both sides, an opening bracket before it, a closing bracket after it, and a dot or an underscore on neither. Text you type stays as typed and sticks to what is next to it, except that a space you type becomes the join character too.
help.separators.example: Drag Show, a dash and Episode code: with Space the name is Show Name - 1x01, and with Dot it is Show.Name.-.1x01. Drag Show, an opening bracket, Year and a closing bracket: Show Name (2020). Type S before Season and E before Episode, and the name is S01E05, with nothing added around the letters.
help.language.title: Language tags
help.language.explanation:
A tag is the language, then optionally the script and the region, joined by hyphens: pt, pt-BR, sr-Latn-RS. The region says how the language is used somewhere (Brazil, Latin America); the script says how it is written (Latin, Cyrillic, Han). Both are optional, and a rule for pt also fits pt-BR tracks.

The choice is a rule on the chip, like keeping or dropping it: it gives the language to every track the chip stands for, in each file of the batch. A season or an episode can make its own choice over the show's.
help.language.example: es-419 is Spanish as used in Latin America (419 is the code of that area). Pick Spanish, then the region Latin America and the Caribbean, or type es-419.

queue.title: Queue
queue.clear_tip: Removes every item from the queue except the one that is running, waiting items included. Nothing on disk changes.
queue.kept: Each item keeps the settings it had when it was added.
queue.status.pausing: Pausing once the running step ends · {count}
queue.note.replaced: {place} was added to the queue again with its settings as they are now: {files}. The waiting item it replaces was removed.
queue.note.clash: {place} was not queued: a file of it is in {item}, which has not finished. Remove that item, or let it end, and add the place again.
queue.refused.changed.one: 1 file changed on disk since it was read, so the place was not queued. It is read again; add the place again.
queue.refused.changed.other: {count} files changed on disk since they were read, so the place was not queued. They are read again; add the place again.
queue.refused.plans: The plan changed while the place was being queued, so it was not queued. Add the place again.
queue.refused.nothing: Nothing in this place can be written, so it was not queued.
queue.refused.error: The place could not be queued: {error}
queue.detail.interrupted: Stopped after {done} of {total} steps. Start goes on with it; each file is checked again first.
queue.detail.failed: {reason} Retry runs the failed steps again with the settings kept when it was added.
queue.detail.changed: {done} of {total} steps written. {left} not written: a file changed on disk after it was queued. Remove the item and add the place again to plan that file as it is now.
queue.detail.cancelled: Cancelled. A file that was being written keeps its original; Retry goes on with the rest.
queue.detail.unreadable: Stored by another version of Showrunner; it can only be removed.
tip.drawer_fold: Fold the drawer away. Jobs and the queue keep running behind it.
tip.library_add: Add a folder of shows or movies to the library. It is only read; nothing on disk changes.
tip.library_refresh: Read the open folders again: files deleted on disk drop out, new ones come in, and choices stay. Only changed files are read.
tip.names_open: Open this track's names, one line per file, to keep or drop a single file's track.
tip.chip_remove: Take this token out of the template (a middle click on the chip does the same). It stays in the palette.
tip.review_open: Open this file's card to see its tracks, defaults, title, names and flags before and after.
tip.rule_pause: Pause this rule without deleting it. A paused rule plans no change.
tip.rule_resume: Turn this rule on again so it plans changes.
tip.rule_edit: Open this rule as a sentence to change what it matches and what it does.
tip.rule_delete: Delete this rule from this place. The plan updates at once; no file changes until Apply.
tip.settings_close: Close Settings and return to the workspace.
tip.token_close: Close the editor and go back to the palette.
tip.token_edit: Change how this token's value is written: a built-in token opens its replace values, a custom one its whole definition.
tip.token_add: Create a custom token from a pattern. It joins the palette.
tip.top_drawer: Show or hide the drawer: the player, jobs, the queue and the log.
tip.top_settings: Open Settings: general, appearance, profiles, programs and shortcuts.
tip.track_drop: Drop this track: the new file leaves it out. Nothing is written until Apply.

workspace.tab_tip.subtitles: Choose what happens to the subtitles: languages, cleanup, sync, translation. The number counts the subtitles planned here and the new files they need.
